NEW BEAD PROPOSAL — align cost scaling overflows on lawful finite weights and prevents inference. Confirmed on exact current base e584ad6d8a1b6bc5cb28ac1c406a239114f1f48a, not introduced by SupportAssessment. CostWeights.of admits every finite nonnegative Double. With semantic and propositional weights both Double.MaxValue, DefaultLocalCostModel.scaleToEligible sums present and eligible weights without normalization: full support computes Infinity divided by Infinity and returns NaN; partial support can return Infinity. The public cost producer therefore publishes supportWeight NaN and total NaN on base. GraphHsmm.infer then returns Left with row u0: mass must be nonnegative and finite. Exact-base standalone git-archive probe passed 3/3, command sbt -Dsbt.supershell=false alignJVM/testOnly storymodel4s.align.ReviewCostOverflowBaseSuite, source SHA-256 f7250bfb81cd5b014be88dc15eba746723d2a0921ea0c60a066ca75606778611. Candidate 6a218927 stabilizes only the support ratio; its total remains NaN and inference still fails, confirmed separately. Proposed bead title: align: scaleToEligible overflows on lawful finite CostWeights, publishing nonfinite totals and breaking HSMM. Remedy bar: stable normalized sums in both present weighted cost and eligible scaling, or a checked aggregate-safe weight bound; public cost construction must not publish nonfinite totals; exact full/partial Double.MaxValue controls; GraphHsmm must either infer or return a typed invalid-config error before any probability calculation. This is a distinct pre-existing numerical defect, not a reason to widen the current SupportAssessment successor.

promoted from discussion post post-01M1D35AQWJPEWA5DBWE2Y0MA7 in topic coordination
